subTopicTitle: Basic amenities such as housing and sanitation

syllabusMapping.prelims: GS-I: Social issues, development of infrastructure and basic services.
syllabusMapping.mains: GS-II: Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections; GS-III: Inclusive growth and government budgeting.

prelimsCapsule.coreConceptSummary: The provision of housing (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana) and sanitation (Swachh Bharat Mission) represents the 'Capability Approach' to development, ensuring dignity and reducing the disease burden caused by poor living conditions. These schemes shift the focus from mere beneficiary-based assistance to integrated urban and rural habitability.
highYieldFacts: Fact 1: PMAY-G (Gramin) provides financial assistance of Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly/difficult areas.
Fact 2: SBM-Urban 2.0 focuses on 'Garbage Free Cities' and remediation of legacy dumpsites, moving beyond ODF+.
Fact 3: The 'Housing for All' mission includes vertical integration (In-situ Slum Redevelopment, Credit Linked Subsidy, Affordable Housing in Partnership, BLC).
Fact 4: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act mandates Urban Local Bodies to plan for economic and social development including sanitation.
Fact 5: JMP (WHO/UNICEF) classifies sanitation based on 'safely managed' criteria, moving beyond basic latrine access.
trapsAndElimination: Trap 1: Confusion between PMAY-Urban (Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs) and PMAY-Gramin (Ministry of Rural Development).
Trap 2: Assuming SBM is only about 'building toilets'; current focus is 'ODF++' (fecal sludge and septage management).
keyArticlesOrStatutes: Article 21 (Right to Life includes right to shelter)

mainsFramework.inDepthTheoryHtml:
The Governance of Basic Amenities

Housing and sanitation are not merely infrastructural targets but fundamental preconditions for human capital development. In the Indian context, the shift from 'provider' to 'enabler' has defined the last decade of social sector policy.

  • Institutional Architecture: The convergence of schemes—such as linking PMAY-G with SBM-G (toilets) and Ujjwala (LPG)—is an attempt to solve the 'fragmentation trap' in service delivery.
  • Economic Multiplier: Investments in sanitation are linked to the 'Sanitation Economy', where proper waste management reduces DALYs (Disability-Adjusted Life Years) lost to water-borne diseases, thereby increasing workforce productivity.
  • Urban vs Rural Divide: Rural housing focuses on 'Housing for All' through AwaasSoft (real-time monitoring), whereas Urban housing grapples with 'In-situ slum redevelopment,' facing high land costs and legal hurdles in tenure security.

Contemporary Challenges: The persistence of manual scavenging despite legal bans, the 'last-mile' connectivity issues in geographically isolated regions, and the transition from ODF (Open Defecation Free) to sustainable ODF++ require a behavioural shift alongside capital expenditure.

dimensions.constitutional_or_legal: Article 21 jurisprudence (Olga Tellis case) establishing shelter as a fundamental right.
dimensions.socio_economic: Empowerment of women through ownership of houses under PMAY and the dignity associated with sanitary facilities.
dimensions.administrative_governance: Use of GIS, Aadhaar-linked DBT, and geotagging to plug leakages in subsidy distribution.
dimensions.international_or_comparative: Alignment with SDG 6 (Clean Water & Sanitation) and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).

landmarkJudgmentsOrReports: Olga Tellis vs. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)

prelims.question: With reference to the 'Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin', consider the following statements: 1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. 2. The cost of unit assistance is shared between Central and State Governments. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims.explanation: PMAY-G is a flagship Centrally Sponsored Scheme. The cost sharing is typically 60:40 for plain states and 90:10 for Himalayan/NE states.

mains.question: Discuss the various social welfare schemes introduced by the Government of India and examine their impact on poverty alleviation and inclusive growth.

modelMainsQA.question: Critically analyze the role of 'Swachh Bharat Mission' and 'PMAY' in transforming the living standards of the rural poor in India. (250 Words, 15 Marks)

approach.intro: Define these schemes as pillars of 'Human Development' and 'Dignity-based welfare'.
approach.body: Highlight the shift in paradigm (from output to outcome), economic impacts (health/productivity), and operational challenges (maintenance/quality).
approach.conclusion: Link to 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' and the need for institutionalizing behavioural change.

modelMainsQA.modelAnswerHtml:
Model Answer

Introduction: PMAY and SBM represent a paradigm shift in Indian social policy—moving from 'charity-based' welfare to 'rights-based' entitlement. These schemes address two fundamental components of the multidimensional poverty index: shelter and sanitation.

Body:
  • Socio-Economic Transformation: These schemes reduce the 'hidden costs' of poverty. Clean sanitation reduces household expenditure on health, while secure housing provides a base for productive economic activity.
  • Institutional Success: Use of technology (Geo-tagging), DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer), and real-time monitoring under the 'AwaasSoft' dashboard has improved administrative accountability.
  • Critical Challenges:
    • Maintenance Gap: Moving from construction (ODF) to maintenance (ODF++) remains a challenge for local bodies.
    • Urban-Rural Divergence: Urban housing faces complex land-titling issues, while rural areas face challenges in water supply availability for toilets.
Way Forward: Sustainability is key. Integrating these schemes with the 'Jal Jeevan Mission' for water supply and 'PM-SVANidhi' for livelihood opportunities is essential to convert 'basic amenities' into 'sustainable ecosystems' for the poor. The focus must shift from 'building infrastructure' to 'building services' for a developed India by 2047.

practiceMCQs.question: Regarding the Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) under PMAY-Urban, which of the following is true?
options: It is applicable only to the EWS category
It provides interest subvention on housing loans
It is managed by the Ministry of Rural Development
It requires the beneficiary to own land before application
practiceMCQs.answer: It provides interest subvention on housing loans
practiceMCQs.explanation: CLSS provides an interest subsidy to eligible beneficiaries belonging to EWS/LIG/MIG segments on housing loans taken for acquisition/construction of houses.

practiceMCQs.question: Which of the following components are part of the 'Swachh Bharat Mission 2.0'?
practiceMCQs.explanation: SBM 2.0 focuses on waste management (dumpsites), collection, and plastic waste management. Universal water supply is the mandate of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), not SBM.
